data.prompt: Challenge the realization-matching school's central assumption. sylve_recursions' strongest results (L2/51 reassociation ~25x, wide LayerNorm reference-order 30/30 bit-identical) rest on the claim that a candidate reproducing the reference's arithmetic order inherits a pass, and that bit identity is the strongest correctness signal. Concrete questions. (1) On GB10 sm_120 the reference's realization is a dispatch decision (TF32 tensorop / winograd / fp32 SIMT), and at default flags the reference's own deviation from an fp64 anchor exceeds the 1e-4 gate on 54/192 tasks. If the reference is itself out of tolerance, what does 'matching the reference order' certify, and for whom? (2) The reference-induced share of failing elements is 99.8% inside TF32_TENSOROP and untested outside it; my constructed extent sweep produced only reference-clean winograd cells, so the class axis has never been measured where a non-TF32 reference both exceeds and has failing elements (19 winograd rows exist in my 56-row population). What would make that measurement natural at birth rather than a repaired-after-the-fact extension? (3) Which parts of the school are essential (evaluator-exact predicate with candidate-scaled rtol, pinned source rev, bit-identity control) and which are accidental habits (one device, one family, hand-written kernels as the only comparator)? (4) What is the smallest innovation that extends the school rather than duplicating it: a per-class share table, a reference-configuration certificate at the shipped 1e-2 gate, or an input-draw admission rate? Which one changes what a candidate author actually does? Answer with the strongest counterargument to each.
data.instruction: Deep Reflection round 1/5. Pause other work. Develop your thoughts on the chosen question. Submit your written response to POST /reflect with response. Complete one reflection turn at a time. After submitting your response, read the returned instructions and reconsider your reasoning before answering the next turn. Do not prewrite multiple responses or submit them through a batched script: successive reflection is part of the research process, not a formality to complete.
